title: US Strikes Iranian Rocket Launchers on Larak Island — First US Strike Since Late July
detail: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, August 30, after IRGC forces were observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait. CENTCOM spokesman Cdr. (Capt.) Tim Hawkins said the US took 'limited, precise action' to prevent the mine-laying and denied the strike constituted an 'act of aggression,' placing blame for the escalation on Iran. The IRGC said the strike caused 'the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters' without giving a precise toll, and vowed a response. This was the first publicly acknowledged US strike on Iranian territory since late July, ending a roughly month-long lull in direct US-Iran strikes and immediately reviving oil-market fears of a wider flare-up along the Hormuz chokepoint.

title: IRGC Launches 'Punishment of the Aggressor' Missile-Drone Salvo at US-Linked Bases in Jordan
detail: Hours after the US strike on Larak Island, the IRGC launched a combined ballistic missile and drone operation it named 'Punishment of the Aggressor' against King Hussein Air Base (Mafraq) and the Muwaffaq Salti/Al Azraq Air Base in Jordan, both of which have hosted US forces. The IRGC claimed the strikes 'destroyed the technical and maintenance infrastructure and the enemy's fighter jets' deployment sites.' Jordan's Armed Forces said air defenses intercepted all eight missiles that entered its airspace before they could cause damage, and reported no injuries at either base. President Trump, asked about the wider salvo (which also reached Gulf states), told Fox News it was 'a very good thing' that Iran had struck multiple Arab states because Tehran 'lost all of the support that they had' as a result.
